h1: The 5 Best Ceramic Air Fryers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Ceramic Air Fryers 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five air fryers with ceramic-coated baskets compared on capacity, cooking functions, presets and price band.
summary: The Cosori TurboBlaze is the best all-round ceramic air fryer, with a 6 quart basket and a PFAS-free ceramic coating. The Cosori Pro LE 5 Qt is the cheaper step down. Nuwave's 8 quart suits big families, the Tastee adds app recipes and 24 presets, and the Chefman 6-in-1 is the roomy budget option.
intro: Ceramic on an air fryer label can mean very different things. Some listings say PFAS-free ceramic coating, while others only say non-stick or non-toxic, and the difference decides whether the basket is actually ceramic. Read the coating line before you read the wattage.

We reviewed eight models and kept the five whose listings name a ceramic coating or ceramic basket. They are ranked on capacity, cooking functions, presets and price band, using the spec sheets alone.

products.name: Cosori TurboBlaze Air Fryer
products.verdict: A 9-in-1 with a PFAS-free ceramic coating at a 6 quart size.
products.description:
The TurboBlaze is a 6 quart, 9-in-1 air fryer with a PFAS-free ceramic coating. It sits in the $100 to $200 band.

It ranks first because it combines a stated PFAS-free coating with the widest function count here. Against the Pro LE it adds capacity (6 quarts instead of 5) at a higher band.

It suits families of three or four who want one machine for most jobs. A 6 quart basket is still compact enough for most counters.
products.skipIf: You cook for a crowd every night.

products.name: Cosori Air Fryer Pro LE 5 Qt
products.verdict: The same 9 functions in a 5 quart body for less.
products.description:
The Pro LE is a 5 quart, 9-in-1 air fryer with a ceramic coating and a shake reminder. It sits in the $50 to $100 band.

It ranks below the TurboBlaze because it is a size smaller and the listing does not say PFAS-free. In return it costs a band less.

Buy it for one to three people. The shake reminder helps with fries and wings.
products.skipIf: You batch cook for four or more.

products.name: Nuwave Brio Plus Air Fryer 8 Qt
products.verdict: An 8 quart basket with a PFAS-free ceramic coating.
products.description:
The Brio Plus offers 8 quarts of space and a PFAS-free ceramic coating, in the $100 to $200 band.

It ranks below the Cosori models because the listing gives fewer details on functions. What you gain is room, since 8 quarts is the largest basket among the Cosoris.

It suits bigger households that cook big batches. It needs more counter space than a 5 or 6 quart.

products.name: Tastee Ceramic Air Fryer
products.verdict: 24 presets, in-app recipes and a dishwasher-safe basket.
products.description:
The Tastee is an 8-in-1, 5.5 quart air fryer with 24 one-touch presets, in-app recipes with a window and a dishwasher-safe non-stick basket. It sits in the $100 to $200 band.

It ranks fourth because you pay the same band as the TurboBlaze for fewer functions, but you get app recipes.

It suits beginners who want presets to guide them. Experienced cooks will use manual controls anyway.

products.name: Chefman Crispinator Air Fryer 6-in-1 with 8 Qt capacity
products.verdict: An 8 quart basket with a ceramic basket, in a lower band.
products.description:
This Chefman has an 8 quart capacity, a nonstick ceramic basket and a viewing window, in the $50 to $100 band.

It ranks last because it lists fewer cooking details than the others. Against the Nuwave 8 Qt it saves a band.

It works for budget buyers who need space. Check the coating wording on the listing, as only the basket is stated as ceramic.
products.skipIf: You want the strongest feature set.

whatMatters.detail: Ceramic is a coating applied to the basket, replacing traditional non-stick chemistry. Some listings say PFAS-free, while others only say non-toxic. Choose a model that names ceramic explicitly. Search the bullet points for the word ceramic.
Capacity in quarts sets how much food fits in one batch. Five quarts feeds two or three, while eight feeds a crowd. Too large wastes counter space. Match it to your household.
A 9-in-1 usually bakes, roasts, reheats and dehydrates as well as air fries. More functions help if you want to replace other appliances. Look at the named modes, not the count alone.
Presets set time and temperature for common foods. They help beginners but can feel limiting. App recipes add guidance. Check how many presets are listed.
A dishwasher-safe basket saves time. Ceramic coatings still need soft sponges. Confirm dishwasher-safe is stated on the listing.

faq.q: Is ceramic better than regular non-stick?
faq.a: Ceramic avoids traditional PTFE-based coatings, which some buyers prefer. Durability varies, so treat it as a preference.
Avoid them on any coated basket. Use silicone or wood.
For two or three people, yes. The Cosori Pro LE fits that need.

faq.q: How do I set up a new air fryer?
faq.a: Wash the basket, run it empty once, and leave space behind it for airflow.

faq.q: How do I clean the basket?
faq.a: Use warm soapy water and a soft sponge unless the manual says dishwasher-safe, as on the Tastee.
Models with a bake function, such as the Chefman 7-in-1 family and the Cosoris, can handle small batches.

finalTake: The Cosori TurboBlaze is the best ceramic air fryer here, balancing a PFAS-free coating, nine functions and a 6 quart basket. The Pro LE is the smart cheaper choice. For crowds, pick the Nuwave if PFAS matters or the Chefman if budget does.
